tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

tools.description: Create a scheduled task. At each occurrence of rrule, prompt is delivered to the target session as a scheduled message from the user. The result includes the task id and the next occurrence as scheduledAt in UTC and scheduledAtLocal in the zone of rrule. After downtime, only the latest missed occurrence is delivered. rrule.description: Supported RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. DTSTART must name an existing local time. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. No SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value. COUNT is at most 1000; use UNTIL for longer rules. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so select clock times with DAILY or WEEKLY plus BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY. Ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Each FREQ period allows at most 10080 candidates before BYSETPOS, which accepts at most 31 values. UNTIL is a UTC instant ending in Z. Example: "DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Singapore:20260901T080000\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1"

target.description: this_session delivers to this session; new_once delivers to the same new session every time, opened at the first delivery; new opens a different new session for every delivery. New sessions use this session's working directory and preset. With this_session or new_once, a delivery waits until the previous one finishes, and only the latest occurrence that passed meanwhile is delivered. Use this_session for reminders and for follow-ups to this conversation; use new_once or new for independent work, such as a recurring report, and whenever the user asks for a new conversation.

The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its name. If you are still online when it finishes, the runtime automatically delivers its completion notice. The notice includes the final answer unless the child sent you a message just before finishing. Use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

## Requirements recap

1. New offline validator `app/core/urls.py::validate_authorization_url(value, *, env, allowed_hosts) -> str | None`. ✅ Present.
2. Rules:

   - strip ✅
   - >2000 → None ✅ (checks after strip; ok)
   - scheme must be `https` ✅
   - dev/test additionally allow `http` only for literal `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` — need examine. The implementation: `elif scheme == "http" and dev_like and dev_local_host: pass`. `dev_local_host` based on normalized hostname (lower, strip trailing dot). So `localhost.` would count as localhost and be allowed in dev. Minor semantic. Also `127.0.0.1` exact. But what about `http://localhost.`? Host normalized to localhost and passes. Hmm, literal requirement presumably means exact. It's minor.
   - reject credentials in URL — implemented after scheme check! Order: scheme validated first, then credentials. Rule requirement doesn't prescribe specific ordering. But there's a subtle issue: for a URL like `https://user:pass@169.254.169.254`, credentials check returns `credentials_in_url` first, so reason is credentials, tests assert that. Fine.
   - reject IP literals in loopback/private/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified ranges (via ipaddress, no DNS) ✅ — but need to verify IP parsing works with hostname. urlsplit's hostname returns without brackets for IPv6; for IPv4 it's in decimal dotted form. `ipaddress.ip_address("127.0.0.1")` works. However, alternate representations like `127.1`, `2130706433`, `0x7f000001` are not recognized by ipaddress — but are they IP literals? Requirement says "reject IP literals in loopback/private/... ranges (via ipaddress, no DNS)". The review instructions explicitly call out checking decimal/octal/hex/shorthand loopback forms like `127.1`, `2130706433`, `0x7f000001`. The implementer acknowledges in report §7.1 that these are not blocked. Is that a spec violation? The controller decision text says "reject IP literals in loopback/private/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified ranges (via ipaddress, no DNS)". `127.1` is not a valid IP literal per ipaddress, but browsers interpret as loopback. Given security intent ("恶意链接不会出现在 API/SSE 里" and bypasses), these alternate loopback encodings are a known bypass. The task review prompt explicitly directs attention to them. Hmm. Need to judge whether this is critical. The prompt says "Pay special attention to: scheme/host bypasses (... decimal/octal/hex/shorthand loopback forms like `127.1`, `2130706433`, `0x7f000001`)". The implementation does NOT reject these. That means `https://127.1/` and `https://2130706433/` pass as "public domain" when they actually resolve to loopback in browsers. Since these are displayed to users as authorization links, clicking them could direct users to loopback services (e.g., local admin interfaces) — a real risk, though the API doesn't fetch them. Is this in-scope per spec? The spec says reject IP literals in loopback/private ranges "via ipaddress". Strictly, `127.1` isn't an IP literal accepted by `ipaddress`. But the security intent... The implementations' own report flags it. I think this is at least Important. Let me think about what the lead/controller decisions state: "reject IP literals in loopback/private/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified ranges (via ipaddress, no DNS)". The mention "via ipaddress" suggests that ipaddress would be the tool; alternate encodings weren't explicitly required. However, the review instructions explicitly ask to check. I should report it and let the lead decide. The implementer disclosed it as a limitation. Given "A2A auth URL back-end whitelist" security purpose, I'd rate Important (should fix) — recommend rejecting hosts that are all-digits/hex or dotted-numeric-only forms, or canonicalize via `socket.inet_aton`-like offline parsing. Actually `ipaddress.IPv4Address("127.1")` fails, but `int` parse + `str` forms. Could use `ipaddress.IPv4Address(int(host, 0))`? `0x7f000001` int(...,0) = 2130706433 works; `2130706433` decimal works; `127.1` = 127.1 not int. Could handle dotted partial forms. Anyway, fix suggestion.

Good. But `localhost` itself handled separately. What about `.internal` covering `internal`? host == "internal" (exact, no leading dot) would not be caught by `.internal` endswith. Hmm `host.endswith(".internal")` — "internal".endswith(".internal") is False. Should `internal` itself be rejected? Line 13 says "拒绝 localhost/*.localhost/*.local/*.internal（dev/test 例外见上）" — implementation allows dev/test exact localhost only, not suffixes; consistent with "例外见上" (the exception above is exact localhost/127.0.0.1). Fine.

Now evaluate whether `_invalid_host_chars` covers unicode whitespace: `ch.isspace()` yes, but host normalized lower. Good.

Another thought: `_normalize_host` uses `rstrip(".")` — strips all trailing dots (e.g., `example.com...`). A hostname with multiple trailing dots is invalid DNS; browsers would likely reject; treating as `example.com` is okay-ish. If allowlist has `example.com`, `example.com...` matches and gets displayed; browser may fail. Not security. Minor.

Another thought: `_normalize_allowed_hosts` does not handle IPv6 bracket or port entries; config docs say host only. Fine.

Another thought: The validator's scheme branch: `scheme == "https"` passes; but URL with scheme "https" and no netloc but path "example.com" host empty → rejected. Good.

Now, is there any path where `task.auth_request` gets populated from another source (e.g., authorize endpoint response)? grep shows only tool.py writes. ✅.

Now check the test for malicious URL asserts audit count exactly 1. If `_audit_auth_url_rejected` were called twice (e.g., polling duplicates), test would catch in this scenario. fine.

Now think about audit failure handling and transaction state: If `write_audit` raises after `db.add` but before commit (e.g., commit failure), the session context manager `__aexit__` will roll back/close; exception caught. Good. If the exception is raised by `get_session_factory()()` (e.g., pool timeout), caught. Good.

But: There is a subtle issue — `except Exception` in `_audit_auth_url_rejected` catches and suppresses, but if the exception is a `BaseException` like `asyncio.CancelledError` (inherits BaseException in 3.8+), it propagates; that's desirable (cancellation). Fine.

Potential issue: `logger.warning(..., exc_info=True)` could leak DB error details, not URL. fine.

Now, the alternate-encoding issue and malformed redaction leak are the main substantive findings. Also maybe the unicode/IDN numeric forms. Let me verify `https://１２７。０。０。１/` behavior quickly to have evidence.

content.text:
Confirmed. So the audit can leak credentials in two ways. Both reachable from a malicious remote agent returning `authorization_url` as a string malformed IPv6 or non-string object. The integration test asserts no `supersecret` only for the well-formed URL path. Critical.

Wait, is `metadata.get("authorization_url")` guaranteed to be a string per A2A spec? The spec expects string, but remote is untrusted; code explicitly handles non-str. So yes.

Fix recommendation: in `tool.py`, only treat `isinstance(raw, str)` for audit prefix; for non-str use reason only (no prefix) or a fixed placeholder; and in `redact_url_for_audit`, sanitize userinfo before truncating using a robust regex independent of urlsplit parsing, e.g. `re.sub(r"(?<=//)[^/?#]*@", "", stripped)`; also strip control/newline chars to prevent log injection. Add tests with `https://user:secret@[::1`, `https://user:secret@[zz]/`, and dict metadata.

Now, is the malformed URL `https://user:supersecret@[::1` accepted? No—rejected and audited. Good.

Now, does the tool's integration test check that `supersecret` not in audit after well-formed creds; yes. But doesn't cover these. Fine.

Now, maybe another issue: In `redact_url_for_audit`, if URL has credentials and is well-formed, it removes them. If URL has *no* parsed credentials but a `@` in the netloc that urlsplit treats as part of hostname? E.g., `https://host%40user:pass@evil.com` → username parsed. Fine.

Now, another Important: alternate IP encodings. Confirm the dev `http://127.1` case: In prod `https`. In dev, `http://127.1` would be rejected as non_https (host not dev_local) — but `https://127.1` accepted in dev/prod. So the bypass is https loopback via numeric form. In prod, `https://127.1` accepted (valid=True), even though `https://127.0.0.1` rejected. That's a clear bypass. Also `https://2130706433`, `https://0x7f000001`, `https://0177.0.0.1`. Test verified.

Could also bypass private ranges, e.g., `https://0xa9fea9fe` (169.254.169.254) or `https://2852039166`; browsers would map to link-local metadata; accepted. So "reject IP literals in link-local/private" is bypassed too. This makes it an explicit rule intent violation, though not via `ipaddress` parsing. I'd mark Important. Could be Critical? The URL isn't fetched server-side; the risk is user clicking. The rule is about not displaying such URLs. The prompt explicitly asks. ### Strengths
- 校验器纯离线：仅依赖 `urllib.parse` + `ipaddress`，未复用会做 DNS 的 `app.core.ssrf`；展示层不会因 DNS 故障抖动。
- 规则实现较细：FQDN 尾点归一化、IPv4-mapped IPv6、控制/空白字符主机、`allowed_hosts` 大小写/空白归一化、按规则返回短 reason，均有利于审计和测试。
- 审计接入点正确：在 `task.auth_request` 赋值、`_persist_task`、SSE emit 之前写独立 session 审计（`write_audit(..., commit=True)` 已核对 `app/core/audit.py:18-42` 签名支持），审计异常被 `try/except Exception` 吞掉并二次 warning，任务状态流转不受影响。
- 测试质量总体好：`tests/test_auth_url_unit.py` 表驱动覆盖正反例/原因/配置属性；集成测试通过 `FakeA2aAgent(authorization_url=...)` 真实注入（`_register_fake(**kwargs)` 已核对会透传），覆盖 SSE、详情 API、审计字段、审计失败不阻断任务、历史脏数据展示不写审计，且默认值保留原正向流程。
- 对改动文件重跑 ruff：`All checks passed!`；注释和用户可见消息为中文，行宽符合要求。

### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
1. **`app/core/urls.py:155-156`（配合 `app/modules/a2a/tool.py:267-273,283`）：畸形 URL 的审计前缀未脱敏**
   - 问题：`urlsplit()` 对非法 IPv6 括号抛 `ValueError` 时直接 `return stripped[:limit]`；同一 URL 在 `evaluate_authorization_url()` 中会被判 `invalid_url` 并触发审计，于是 `user:secret@` 原样进入 warning 日志和审计 `detail.url_prefix`。
   - 影响：远程 Agent 是不可信输入，可主动构造 `https://user:supersecret@[::1` 让凭据落审计；违反控制器“detail 绝不落凭据”的硬约束，现有测试只覆盖了格式正确 URL 的脱敏。
   - 修复：在 `except ValueError` 分支也先剥离 userinfo（例如对原文执行 `re.sub(r"//[^/?#]*@", "//", value)` 后再截断），或统一在截断前做一次不依赖 `urlsplit` 成功的脱敏；补单测覆盖 `https://user:pass@[::1`、`@[::1]x`、`@[zz]`。
2. **`app/modules/a2a/tool.py:586-588`（配合 `app/core/urls.py:150-161`）：非字符串 metadata 被字符串化后泄漏**
   - 问题：`authorization_url` 不是字符串时被 `str()` 化；`redact_url_for_audit()` 对 `{'authorization_url': 'https://user:supersecret@169.254.169.254/'}` 这种字符串无法识别内嵌 URL/userinfo，整段写入审计前缀（已实测 `supersecret` 可见）。
   - 影响：远程 Agent 可用嵌套对象绕过 `C1` 的脱敏，同样违反“绝不落凭据”；旧实现本来就会字符串化存储，但本任务新增的审计承诺必须成立。
   - 修复：审计只接受原始 `str`（非字符串时用固定占位或只写 reason，不做 `str(value)`）；或在 `redact_url_for_audit` 中对任意字符串先用正则剥离 `//...@` 片段。补单测：metadata 为 dict 时审计 detail 不含凭据。

#### Important (Should Fix)
1. **`app/core/urls.py:39-41,125-132`：回环/私网 IP 的非标准写法可绕过**
   - 问题：仅靠 Python `ipaddress` 识别标准字面量，浏览器会进一步归一化的 `127.1`、`2130706433`、`0x7f000001`、`0177.0.0.1`、`0xa9fea9fe`、`%31%32%37.0.0.1`、`%2e` 尾点、反斜杠 `\/`、全角数字/句点等全部放行（均实测返回原值）。
   - 影响：远程 Agent 仍可把等价的回环/云元数据链接下发到 API/SSE；与“恶意链接不会出现在 API/SSE 里”的验收目标不符。控制器原始措辞是“via `ipaddress`”，因此这可视为字面合规但安全意图缺口；实现者已把它列为后续项，建议本任务修复或由控制器明确接受风险。
   - 修复：在 IP 判断前做浏览器一致的主机归一化：`unquote` 百分号编码、`idna` 编码、反斜杠按 `/` 处理或直接拒绝、识别 1–4 段十进制/十六进制/八进制 IPv4 缩写并转成 32 位地址后再走 `_blocked_ip_reason`；对非标准/非 ASCII 数字主机可选择直接拒绝。补表驱动用例覆盖上述写法；若控制器判定超范围，需在文档中写明并加 `allowed_hosts` 缓解说明。

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
